dc86b61ab1849e33a5f44742e43098af203a0e1e: Jeizinen is a modest-sized, little-known resort — 8 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and lift queues that barely exist. Jeizinen's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Jeizinen's altitude (1,519 m at the bottom, 2,193 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow cover through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Jeizinen is clearly high: 55€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you set off. In short: Jeizinen doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
